The framework's `Concept` is the interface in `openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-api/src/types/concept-resource.ts`, re-exported through `@openmrs/esm-framework`. Only two chart declarations import it directly from the framework:

1. **`postOrders.ts`**: the `ObsPayload` interface uses `concept: Concept | string` as the observation payload sent when posting encounters. This is the most likely place for a behaviour change to matter, since it builds the request body.
2. **`obs-table-horizontal.component.tsx`**: `HorizontalTableProps` takes `concepts: Array<Concept>`, and the `Cell` component takes the same `concepts` prop. Both feed the horizontal obs table's cell rendering and editing.

The other files that use the name `Concept` (`helper.tsx`, `usePanelData.tsx`, `visit-notes.resource.ts`, `form-data-source.service.ts`, and several chart `types` files) import or define their own local `Concept` types, so a framework change would not reach them.

This is not exhaustive for indirect exposure. Many chart declarations use framework types such as `Obs`, `Order`, `Drug` and `Person`, whose `concept` or `causeOfDeath` fields are typed as the framework `Concept`. I did not enumerate those, and I did not check the framework's `Obs`/`Order` declarations for the chart uses. I also did not read the full `Cell` component body, so I've cited only its props declaration.
